recipes.name: Bacon Wrapped Pesto Chicken
ingredients_raw: 6 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - pounded flat
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

Lay a chicken breast out flat, and sprinkle with salt and black pepper. Spread pesto sauce over the chicken breast, and roll the chicken breast in a slice of bacon, securing the roll with toothpicks. Lay the rolled chicken breast into a 9x9-inch baking dish. Repeat with remaining chicken breasts. Pour the vegetable oil over the chicken breasts.

Bake in the preheated oven until the chicken is no longer pink inside and the bacon is crisp, about 30 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of a roll should read at least 160 degrees F (70 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Bacon Wrapped Pesto Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Celebrate summer's bumper crop of basil with this easy chicken dish of pesto-flavored chicken breasts wrapped in bacon. Make your own pesto or buy it--either way, it's delicious.

review.reviewBody: This was quite a tasty dish, something a bit more unique for the not so every day dinner! I did add some Parmesan cheese and garlic powder. Just sprinkled the garlic powder with fresh crushed pepper sprinkled on the chicken and mixed the cheese with the pesto, very yummy!! I also omitted the salt, I had pre-packaged pesto which was pretty salty. I also did not use the full 1/4 cup of olive oil, because it seemed like a lot, just sprinkled it over the chicken before baking. Not too many changes but they suited my family's tastes, as I am sure the recipe is just fine as written. A great way to use up extra pesto and chicken!!!

Used thin bacon to wrap. Added garlic powder to the pesto and chopped up sun dried tomatoes packed in oil. sprinkled with Gorgonzola cheese. Rolled in grainy mustard and Panko crumbs and then the bacon. My guest loved them.

A very delicious and easy to make recipe! My children loved it...even my one that doesn't like meat!!! My one pesto rule is to only use Buitoni brand...it is superior to any other pesto I have ever had! When making, I ran out of salt so I just used seasoning salt, but otherwise followed the recipe. I have one issue with it...the 1/2 cup of vegetable oil is way too much. The dish is swimming in oil at the end. Instead, next time, I will lightly coat the bottom of the baking dish and rub the oil onto the chicken.

Great chicken dish. I cooked it in my Dutch oven. After I browned the chicken and removed the chicken. I left the sauce from browning the chicken and added 1/2 diced White onion with diced garlic. I sautéed adding chardonnay. Layered pesto bacon topped chicken back in the Dutch oven. I slow cooked it for an hour at 350• in the covered Dutch oven. It was awesome.

Great recipe. Like most, I modified it just slightly. Since I was cooking for several people, I made a large portion. I used a 9 x 12 baking dish and layered it with some home made pesto. I decided not to wrap the bacon around the chicken, nor did I roll or "fill" the chicken. Instead, I placed chicken tenderloins on top of the pesto and then spread additional pesto on top of the chicken (generous portion), followed by shredded parmesan cheese. Then I layered thick-sliced bacon on top of it all. I poured some extra lite virgin olive oil on top. I cooked it uncovered at 400 for about 30 minutes, then removed it from the oven and drained most of the oil that accumulated so that the bacon would crisp. I upped the oven temperature to 450 and cooked it for another 20 minutes. Came out great. Chicken was incredibly moist. I also cooked some fettuccine with pesto and placed the chicken on top of the fettuccine when serving the dish. A sure hit! Thanks for the recipe.

I made it using Sweet Basil and Pecan Pesto and thick cut Hickory smoked bacon. It turned out superb and was a big hit. One other thing that I did differently was I cooked them on my charcoal pit and smoked them. Cooked for about 60 min. on a low heat about 270 and then for the last 30 min. I increased the heat to crisp the bacon a bit. You also have to turn the breasts several times to get an even brown and properly crisp the bacon.

Great recipe, easy to make, and the family loves it. Only difference is that our oven was out of commission for a while, so I started cooking it on a propane grill. Bacon comes out nice and crispy and the fat drips off. I also add a little of bit of shredded cheese with the pesto because we are a bunch of cheese freaks over here.

After reading the reviews, I partially cooked the bacon before wrapping. It was a little less pretty but the bacon came out crispy. I had chicken tenders on hand so I used those, and let them sit in a sealed bag with pesto for about 3 hours. I also skipped the oil pour, instead spraying the wrapped chicken with cooking spray just before baking, and sprinkling some parmesan over the whole thing. Delicious!

I made this with halved breast fillets. I tenderized, sprinkled them in paprika and then smeared a heaping tablespoon of pesto on each flat-half. Then I cut some strips of canned roasted red pepper and placed them perpendicular to the fillet on top of the pest. I sprinkled mozzarella and goat cheese on top of that and then ground some fresh pepper on everything. I then rolled my fillets (like a swiss roll) and began to wrap the bacon.

It was very tricky to wrap the bacon, I had thick sliced bacon on hand, which made it more difficult to stretch around the rolled breasts. I ended up using large bamboo skewers to secure the bacon to the breasts, about two skewers per breast. 

I placed them in a raised roasting pan and baked at 350 for 40 minutes, then broiled about 10 minutes, rotating them for an even brown. 

They came out well. I like a lot of flavor, which they kind of lacked. They could have used more tang, perhaps more goat cheese, or maybe stuffing some kalamata olives? I love salt so those might be my additions next go around.

I did not add extra oil. The chicken was slightly dry.

Whole family loved it! Precooked bacon so it was a little crispier in the end, used boneless skinless thighs and added shredded cheese in the middle of the chicken before topping with pesto and wrapping in bacon. Skipped the veggie oil and used the bacon fat. Delicious!

I made the chicken and bacon recipe. But I used regular fresh chicken tenders wrapped in bacon and cooked on the grill. I did put foil down because of how greasy the bacon is. Right before almost done - took foil off and browned them up a little more.They were fantastic. Highly recommend.
This was an excellent recipe. I made some fettuccini on the side with a pesto and a fresh green salad.
Adaptations: For more flavor, add Italian Seasoning to the Salt & Pepper or (optional) marinate the overnight in Italian Dressing.
Easy to make. Did not brown. Tasted very good!
Cooked exactly per the recipe. Turned out dry. Sadly I won't be making this again

Used boneless, skinless thighs. Spread red pesto sauce and a slice of cheese. Didn’t roll very well (too small) so folded in half and secured with toothpicks. Precooked the bacon a bit and just laid slices on top rather than wrapping. Eas excellent. But breasts might be better for this particular recipe.
It was GREAT everyone loved it only change was I grated some Habinaro cheese over the pesto for a little kick
It tasted amazing! The chicken definitely needs to be cut thin. The only change I made was to add a slice of mozzarella cheese inside the roll. That gave it added flavor.
Everyone is right. Bacon does not crisp. Love the smoky flavor the bacon gives but for me I will add more pesto and cheese, Maybe swiss.
